QUESTION:
Which setting picks the algorithm the component that decides which consumer reads which partition uses to shrink data?

DOCUMENTATION EXCERPTS:
[d0707] config | partitioner.compression | version 4.x
# `partitioner.compression`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Compression codec that the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written uses for stored or transferred data.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | enum: none | lz4 | zstd |
| Default | `none` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Default changed | in 4.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.compression` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
compression = "none"
```

---

# `partitioner.enabled`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Turns the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written on or off.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | boolean |
| Default | `true` |
| Available since | 1.1 |
| Component | partitioner |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.enabled` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
enabled = true
```

---

# `partitioner.compression` (PaderQueue 3.x)

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 3.x.

Compression codec that the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written uses for stored or transferred data.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | enum: none | lz4 | zstd |
| Default | `lz4` |
| Available since | 1.2 |
| Component | partitioner |

## Tuning advice

Measure before you tune. Increase or decrease `partitioner.compression` in small steps and observe the effect for at least one day.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
compression = "lz4"
```

# `partitioner.buffer_bytes`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Size of the in-memory buffer used by the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, in bytes.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer (bytes) |
| Default | `16777216` |
| Available since | 2.0 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | bytes |
| Default changed | in 3.0 (see release notes) |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.buffer_bytes` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
buffer_bytes = 16777216
```

# `partitioner.batch_size`

> Configuration reference for PaderQueue 4.x (current).

Number of messages the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written processes together in one batch.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | integer |
| Default | `256` |
| Available since | 2.3 |
| Component | partitioner |
| Unit | messages |

## When to change it

The default works for most deployments. Change `partitioner.batch_size` only if you observe problems with the partitioner that decides into which partition a message is written, for example in the metrics dashboard.

Set it in `paderqueue.toml`:

```toml
[partitioner]
batch_size = 256
```

response.content: `partitioner.compression` selects the compression codec. In PaderQueue 4.x, the available codecs are `none`, `lz4`, and `zstd` (default: `none`).
